{{nihongo|'''Nagahatabe Shrine'''|長幡部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

=== Origin ===
The founding year is unknown. According to shrine tradition, its origin is that immigrant-descended clans with advanced weaving techniques enshrined the weaving deity "Ame-no-Hatsuchio-no-Mikoto" as guardian deity at Nishimatoba-nishi, Aza-Miya, on the south bank of the Kanna River<ref name="Nagahatabe Shrine origin">Commemorative booklet for the 62nd Ise Grand Shrine rebuilding, ''Nagahatabe Shrine Origin''</ref>. "Nagahata" refers to a kind of silk fabric called "ashiginu," and the shrine name "Nagahatabe" indicates the artisan group "Nagahatabe clan" that wove it. Regarding the origin of that clan, the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}} says it descends from {{ill|Kami Ōne|Q119380336|qid=Q119380336}}, ancestor of {{ill|Motosu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11520234|qid=Q11520234}} ({{ill|Minozaki no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11358204|qid=Q11358204}}), while ''Asaue clan genealogy and estate record'' says Ame-no-Hatsuchio-no-Mikoto was the ancestral deity. Separate from the ancient native Nagahatabe clan, among the "{{ill|Seven-Surname Han People|Q17211949|qid=Q17211949}}" who came from {{ill|Daifang Commandery|Q704994|qid=Q704994}} on the Korean Peninsula with {{ill|Achi no Omi|Q11657596|qid=Q11657596|lt=King Achi}} in June of {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 4 (785) to escape warfare, there was also a clan of the "Kō" surname<ref name="Shoku Nihongi">''{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}'', entry for June of {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 4 (785)</ref><ref name="Shinsen Shōjiroku">'''''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', Vol. 23, lost text in entry on the Sakagami clan'''
::''In the reign of Emperor Ōjin, avoiding turmoil in the homeland, [they] came to Japan with mother, wife, children, younger brother Sensenkōtoku, and Han people of seven surnames...''
::(full quotation omitted in translation context)
</ref>.

In {{ill|Ten'ei|Q1193915|qid=Q1193915}} 1 (1110), flooding of the Kanna River washed away the shrine grounds, so it was moved from Nishimatoba of Aza-Miya to present Ōaza Nagahama<ref name="Nagahatabe Shrine origin"/>.

In June of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 10 (1582), Kami District of Musashi became the battlefield of the "{{ill|Battle of Kanagawa|Q1058786|qid=Q1058786}}" between {{ill|Takigawa Kazumasu|Q953624|qid=Q953624}}, retainer of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}, and Hōjō forces led by {{ill|Hōjō Ujimasa|Q736948|qid=Q736948}}. War fire destroyed shrine buildings and old documents<ref name="Nagahatabe Shrine origin"/>.

In the Edo period, because the Niu deity was interpreted as earth, water, fire, metal, and wood deities, it was called "Goshonomiya"<ref name="Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō">''Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō'', Nagahama-shimogō village</ref>.

In Meiji 5, the shrine name was restored from "Nagahata Goshamiya" to the current "Nagahatabe Shrine"<ref name="Nagahatabe Shrine origin"/>.

=== Precinct shrines ===
Merged before Meiji.
* Kubo Inari Shrine<ref name="Kōtaijinja origin">Commemorative booklet for the 62nd Ise Grand Shrine rebuilding, ''Kōtaijinja Origin''</ref>  
Merged in Meiji 41. "Kōtaijinja" was returned in Shōwa 21 (1946) to its former site in Kubo at strong local request.
* Kubo Kōtaijinja (deity) Ōhirume-no-Muchi-no-Mikoto<ref name="Kōtaijinja origin"/>
* Aza-Miya Niu-sha
* Aza-Miya Inari-sha
: subordinate shrine of Aza-Miya Niu-sha

=== Access ===
* From JR {{ill|Takasaki Line|Q1346657|qid=Q1346657}}{{ill|Jimbohara Station|Q845133|qid=Q845133}}, take Kamisato town bus Komugicchi-go (south route) bound for "Unicus" from "Nishihara-chō" stop; get off at final stop "Minami Gomyō Kōkaidō," then 15 min walk.
* From JR {{ill|Takasaki Line|Q1346657|qid=Q1346657}}{{ill|Honjō Station (Saitama)|Q844906|qid=Q844906}}, take Asahi Bus bound for "Kansen Sōgō Shisho"; get off at "Sanchō," 30 min walk.
* From JR {{ill|Hachikō Line|Q1372071|qid=Q1372071}}{{ill|Tanshō Station|Q845044|qid=Q845044}}, take Asahi Bus bound for "Honjō Station South Exit"; get off at "Sanchō," 30 min walk.
